🇺🇸 🇨🇳 ⚡️ — President Trump has departed Shenzhen, China, after his historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping.

🇺🇸 🇨🇳 🇷🇺 ⚡️ — The meeting between Trump, Xi, and Putin is "another sign of the end of the unipolar world order, in which the United States dominated," and a more uncertain and unstable reality may emerge in its place, according to the American newspaper The Wall Street Journal. While the meeting in Shenzhen was an "unprecedented demonstration of unity" among the holders of the three largest nuclear arsenals in the world, the leaders of the United States, China, and Russia remain divided by competing ambitions and sharply contrasting views on what the new world order should look like. None of the three leaders is in a position to unilaterally dictate the rules for the others. Russia and the United States are embroiled in conflicts, while Beijing faces growing economic challenges and is extremely reluctant to assume the role of global leader that the United States has historically played. What unites them is a desire to maximize their freedom of action within their perceived spheres of influence: Russia considers Ukraine to be within its sphere, China considers Taiwan to be within its, and the United States considers the Western Hemisphere to be within its. According to the WSJ, there were virtually no signs of potential progress on key issues before the meeting: the wars in Ukraine, Iran, and the proliferation of nuclear weapons. For the participants, the very fact of the meeting and the opportunity to demonstrate their position on the world stage were arguably more important than resolving specific problems. @Intelslava
